title: Finite label sections form a subgroup on an etale neighborhood
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G$ an abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $U$ an etale object [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], $S$ a finite set, and $e:|G|_U\simeq\underline S$ a constant set-sheaf chart [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Given $x\in U$, there exist an etale $V\to U$, $v\in V$ mapping to $x$, and a set-sheaf isomorphism $e_S:\underline S\simeq |G|_V$ on the localized small etale site at the composite $A=(V\to Y)$. Let $t:S\to G(V)$ be the component at the terminal object of the constant-presheaf sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] followed by $e_S$. Then $t$ is injective, some label maps to zero, for each $a,b\in S$ some label maps to $t(a)+t(b)$, and for each $a\in S$ some label maps to $-t(a)$. The conclusion specifies no group structure on $S$ and no natural transformation of abelian presheaves.

proof.text: Use the inverse set chart to obtain label sections at the terminal object of the localized site at U. Form the finite family indexed by Unit plus (S times S) plus S: zero, all pairwise sums, and all negatives. Map them into the constant set sheaf using the chart. Apply the finite-family section lifting theorem to obtain a single covering sieve. Its lift equations, the inverse chart identities and naturality show that the label image on every nondegenerate covering member contains zero and is closed under addition and negation. The label-injectivity clause gives injectivity on each such member.

Translate that covering sieve from Over U to the small etale site using Sieve.overEquiv and mem_over_iff. The small etale topology definition gives a jointly surjective cover inside it. Choose a member V and a point v above x. Its composite object A over Y lies in the sieve; if its empty sieve were covering, the jointly surjective cover inside that empty sieve would have a member over v, a contradiction.

Restrict the inverse original set chart along Over.map(A to U). The canonical sheafification restriction isomorphism identifies its source with the constant sheaf at the same set S. Compose with pushforwardOverMapIso to identify the target with the underlying set sheaf of G restricted directly to A. The unit-compatibility identity, evaluated at the terminal object over A, identifies its label map with the map on the covering member already treated. Transfer injectivity and the three image-closure properties along this equality.
